solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Group hiding rum around racing enclosure (7)

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so the group holds the other piece within it
'around' as in turned around: ODD faces the other way and reads DDO

annotation.surface: A gang smuggling rum past the racecourse enclosure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink being hidden, but here it is the adjective meaning strange.
annotation.definitionFit: The paddock is the enclosure where horses are paraded before a race.

entries.clue: Test site doctor about to catch itinerant on cycle (7,6)

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'about turn': the doctor turns to face the other way, so GP reads PG
to catch something is to take hold of it, so PG closes round ROVING
in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner, a family doctor
a round = a cycle, as of events

annotation.surface: A doctor at a testing site trying to catch a wandering cyclist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On cycle' reads as riding a bike; it actually puts ROUND after the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A proving ground is a place where weapons, vehicles or ideas are tested.

entries.clue: City roads essentially cleared prior to retreat (7)

indicators.note: the essence, the middle, of the word is removed
in a down clue, the first piece comes before the next

blocks.note: DRIVES = roads; clearing its centre (IV) leaves DR…ES

annotation.surface: City roads, mostly cleared of traffic, before an army pulls back.
annotation.walkthrough: The roads are DRIVES, not ROADS itself; take out its middle two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Saxon capital on the Elbe is one city among many.

entries.clue: Island supporting nomads periodically? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, IS sits underneath and holds the rest up
something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at every other step

annotation.surface: An island that keeps desert wanderers going from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an oasis is an island of green in the desert that sustains nomads now and then.
annotation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, an island in a sea of sand where travellers stop.

entries.clue: Require castle guards to be deeply involved (4-4)

indicators.note: the castle surrounds the other piece, as if guarding it

blocks.note: a keep = the central tower of a castle

annotation.surface: Castle guards required to get thoroughly caught up in something.
annotation.walkthrough: KEEP stands for the whole castle here, and NEED goes between its K and EEP.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: standing in something up to your knees becomes being thoroughly caught up in an affair.

entries.clue: Alert when bishop hides minute snack (6)

indicators.note: the bishop covers up the minute, taking its place

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation, put in its place

annotation.surface: A bishop sneaking a tiny snack while he's alert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny snack', but it is the time unit M, which B replaces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a light bite of food, the kind of small snack you pick at.

entries.clue: Fanatic with stone climbing tree (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word goes upward, reading back to front

blocks.note: a nut = an enthusiast, a fanatic

annotation.surface: An obsessive climbing a tree with a rock in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone' is a precious stone, not a rock.
annotation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is the tropical evergreen tree whose seed gives the spice.

entries.clue: Retired sailor at home having name scratched in sea vessel (4-5)

indicators.note: withdrawn, so turned back: AB goes into reverse
N, for name, is struck out

blocks.note: marine = of the sea; minus N gives MARIE

annotation.surface: A retired sailor at home, scratching his name into a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sea vessel' reads as a ship; the vessel is a kitchen pan, and 'sea' gives MARINE.
annotation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a pan of hot water in which a smaller vessel sits to cook gently.

entries.clue: Try piercing wrinkles in tongues (7)

indicators.note: the try goes into the middle of the wrinkles

annotation.surface: Having a tongue pierced among the wrinkles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongues' means languages, not the body part the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: Lingoes are languages, informally, and tongues are languages too.

entries.clue: Vesper not moved out of capital? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are moved around

annotation.surface: A Vesper cocktail sitting unmoved, far from the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to be a city; it is money, and the question mark flags the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who has overspent has run out of money, out of capital.

entries.clue: Naughty people removing clothing in private (5)

indicators.note: the outside letters, which clothe the word, are stripped off

blocks.note: sinners = naughty people; remove the outside S and S

annotation.surface: Wicked people undressing behind closed doors.
annotation.walkthrough: Stripping is the instruction: SINNERS loses its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones, kept within.

entries.clue: Run excited VIP to secret European exhibition (13)

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up

annotation.surface: An excited celebrity dashing to a hush-hush European show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' sits beside 'excited' as if the VIP is running, but it is the single letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: A retrospective is an exhibition surveying an artist's whole career.

entries.clue: Runner wearing uniform arrested by officer (5)

indicators.note: U is held inside DS, as a suspect by a police officer

blocks.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'
U = uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A fleeing runner in uniform caught by a police officer.
annotation.walkthrough: A runner is a crossword river; the Indus flows through Pakistan.
annotation.definitionFit: A river runs, so a runner stands for a river such as the Indus.

entries.clue: Dish finally lined with sheets by Oscar in club (9)

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'lined' is used
Oscar is in the club in the plain sense of being inside it, so O sits within BAT

blocks.note: O = Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A dish lined with paper at a club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is not food but slang for an attractive person.
annotation.definitionFit: A dish and a dreamboat are both informal words for a very attractive person.

entries.clue: Note anxiety beginning to ease next to River Clyde? (8)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so 'beginning to ease' is E

blocks.note: G, a note of the scale

annotation.surface: Soothing a worry beside Scotland's River Clyde.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River Clyde' looks like one unit, the Glasgow river; split them, and Clyde is Clyde Barrow of Bonnie and Clyde, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Clyde Barrow was a notorious 1930s American gangster, so he is an example.

entries.clue: Cutting last of rations when beset by cold (9)

indicators.note: the last of anything is its final part, and the last of a word is its final letter
AS is surrounded by ARCTIC

annotation.surface: Cutting the last of the rations during a freezing spell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' seems to be reducing the rations; it is the adjective, as in a cutting remark.
annotation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is sharp and wounding, as a sarcastic one is.

entries.clue: Picture old servant taking Conservative to port (6)

indicators.note: to take someone in is to hold them inside, so the old servant takes C into its middle
port is the left side, so in an across clue everything runs leftward, back to front

blocks.note: a serf = a medieval servant bound to the land

annotation.surface: An old servant bringing a Tory to the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' is not a harbour but the left-hand side of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A fresco is a picture painted on wet plaster.

entries.clue: Enjoy drug with a lot of strong drink (8)

indicators.note: most but not all: the last letter goes

blocks.note: STIFF = strong, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Enjoying drugs along with plenty of hard liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strong drink' reads as one phrase; 'strong' is STIFF and 'drink' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A digestif is a drink taken after a meal to aid digestion.

entries.clue: Heartless soldier recalled sound of his weapon? (6)

indicators.note: the central letter is removed
called back, so read back to front

blocks.note: a trooper = a soldier; losing its middle O gives TROPER

annotation.surface: A callous soldier remembering the noise his gun made.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'his' in the definition points back to the soldier, which is why it ends with a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A report is the loud bang of a gun going off.

entries.clue: Extract oaf trapped by knight’s boy (7)

indicators.note: the oaf is held inside the page

blocks.note: a page = a boy serving a knight
an ass = a fool, an oaf

annotation.surface: A knight's servant boy catching a clumsy fool and dragging him out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extract' is the noun, a passage from a book, not the verb the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A passage is a short extract from a text or piece of music.

entries.clue: Duck spied running across interior of nests (8)

indicators.note: the letters run into a new order
the anagram lies across the other piece, surrounding it
the interior of a thing is its inside, so the word's inside letters are kept and its ends dropped

annotation.surface: A duck seen scuttling across between its nests.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird among the nests; it is the verb, to dodge.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for evading something by moving aside, as a boxer avoids a punch.

entries.clue: Monkey cheers male artist up outside of inn (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, RA reads upward, back to front
the outside of a word is its shell, the first and last letters, with the inside thrown away

blocks.note: ta = thanks, cheers, in British slang

annotation.surface: A monkey toasting a male painter outside a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: Ta is British informal thanks, the same sense 'cheers' has in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey.

entries.clue: Revealing agent providing cover for Asian leader (6)

indicators.note: SPY wraps round the leader, covering him

blocks.note: Kim Jong Un, leader of North Korea

annotation.surface: An agent who exposes things while acting as cover for an Asian ruler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' sounds like exposing secrets; it describes clothing that shows a lot of skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Clothes cut from so little fabric show a lot of the body.

entries.clue: Relative using shelter instead of Charlie for free (9)

indicators.note: a word using a new part takes it on board as a working component
'instead of' means in place of, so the new piece fills the slot the old letter vacates

blocks.note: C = Charlie in the NATO alphabet, removed
a shack = a rough shelter, put in its place

annotation.surface: A relative living in a shack rather than paying Charlie, for nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free' reads as 'at no cost'; it is the verb, to release.
annotation.definitionFit: To unshackle is to remove someone's chains, to free them.

entries.clue: Firm MGM instructs can’t initially gag producer (5)

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so each word gives only its start, its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of MGM Instructs Can't

annotation.surface: A film studio ordering that a producer mustn't be muzzled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gag' suggests silencing someone; here it is a joke, and a gag producer is a comedian.
annotation.definitionFit: A comic is a comedian, someone who produces gags, or jokes.

entries.clue: Interpose one metal after another briefly (3,2)

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so one metal follows the other in the answer

annotation.surface: Putting one metal after another in a quick process.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' says the second metal appears as its chemical symbol; copper's is Cu.
annotation.definitionFit: Breaking into a conversation or queue puts you between others, which is what interpose means.

entries.clue: Outline of slug that’s escaped from trap (5)

indicators.note: a trap is slang for a mouth, so the word is one that has come out of the mouth: spoken

blocks.note: a slug = a swig of drink, a draught

annotation.surface: The silhouette of a slug that has got out of a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden pest; it is a gulp of drink. 'Trap' is slang for a mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
annotation.definitionFit: A draft is a first outline of a piece of writing or a plan.

entries.clue: Bones gathered by Jack visiting exposed basin (9)

indicators.note: 'by' as in 'close by': MET is placed right next to the rest
a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so TAR goes inside ASI
the outer letters are stripped away

annotation.surface: Bones collected by a sailor calling at an open harbour basin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gathered by' looks like a passive link; it is MET followed by the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: The metatarsi are the bones of the foot between ankle and toes.

entries.clue: Every single Yankee faced with parking fine (6)

indicators.note: P goes at the front, facing the rest

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs
Y = Yankee in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Every American driver hit with a parking ticket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a parking penalty; it is the adjective, meaning just great.
annotation.definitionFit: Peachy means excellent, just fine.

entries.clue: Backing of piano Anne regularly scored before church (7)

indicators.note: every other letter is struck out
the first piece comes before CE

blocks.note: the even letters of oF pIaNo AnNe

annotation.surface: Anne's piano accompaniment, written out as a score for church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' and 'scored' suggest music; backing is money, and 'scored' means crossed out.
annotation.definitionFit: Financial backing is finance, money put up for a venture.
